From 9d98aa088386aee3db1b7b60b800c0fde0654a4a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Uros Bizjak <ubizjak@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2024 20:55:29 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] x86/bpf: Fix IP after emitting call depth accounting
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Adjust the IP passed to `emit_patch` so it calculates the correct offset
for the CALL instruction if `x86_call_depth_emit_accounting` emits code.
Otherwise we will skip some instructions and most likely crash.

Fixes: b2e9dfe54be4 ("x86/bpf: Emit call depth accounting if required")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/20230105214922.250473-1-joanbrugueram@gmail.com/
Co-developed-by: Joan Bruguera Micó <joanbrugueram@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Joan Bruguera Micó <joanbrugueram@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Uros Bizjak <ubizjak@gmail.com>
Cc: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Cc: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240401185821.224068-2-ubizjak@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>

diff --git a/arch/x86/net/bpf_jit_comp.c b/arch/x86/net/bpf_jit_comp.c
index a7ba8e178645..e55745f512e1 100644
--- a/arch/x86/net/bpf_jit_comp.c
+++ b/arch/x86/net/bpf_jit_comp.c
@@ -480,7 +480,7 @@ static int emit_call(u8 **pprog, void *func, void *ip)
 static int emit_rsb_call(u8 **pprog, void *func, void *ip)
 {
 	OPTIMIZER_HIDE_VAR(func);
-	x86_call_depth_emit_accounting(pprog, func);
+	ip += x86_call_depth_emit_accounting(pprog, func);
 	return emit_patch(pprog, func, ip, 0xE8);
 }
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/net/bpf_jit_comp.c`**
   - The line `x86_call_depth_emit_accounting(pprog, func);` was modified to `ip += x86_call_depth_emit_accounting(pprog, func);`.
   - This change adjusts the instruction pointer (`ip`) by adding the return value of `x86_call_depth_emit_accounting` to it, ensuring that the correct offset is calculated for the subsequent `CALL` instruction.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `bpf_jit_comp.c` directly addresses a bug related to the handling of the instruction pointer after the call depth accounting is emitted. By updating the `ip` variable, the patch ensures that the correct offset is used when emitting the `CALL` instruction, preventing potential crashes that could occur if instructions are skipped. This change is a fix for the issue introduced in a previous commit (`b2e9dfe54be4`), which added the call depth accounting feature.

x86/bpf: Fix IP after emitting call depth accounting
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Adjust the IP passed to `emit_patch` so it calculates the correct offset
for the CALL instruction if `x86_call_depth_emit_accounting` emits code.
Otherwise we will skip some instructions and most likely crash.

Fixes: b2e9dfe54be4 ("x86/bpf: Emit call depth accounting if required")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/20230105214922.250473-1-joanbrugueram@gmail.com/
Co-developed-by: Joan Bruguera Micó <joanbrugueram@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Joan Bruguera Micó <joanbrugueram@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Uros Bizjak <ubizjak@gmail.com>
Cc: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Cc: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240401185821.224068-2-ubizjak@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the instruction pointer (`ip`) after the call depth accounting code was emitted. The original code did not update the `ip` variable to account for the additional instructions generated by `x86_call_depth_emit_accounting`, leading to an incorrect offset for the subsequent `CALL` instruction and potentially causing the program to skip instructions or crash.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int emit_rsb_call(u8 **pprog, void *func, void *ip)
 {
 	OPTIMIZER_HIDE_VAR(func);
-	x86_call_depth_emit_accounting(pprog, func);
+	ip += x86_call_depth_emit_accounting(pprog, func);
 	return emit_patch(pprog, func, ip, 0xE8);
 }

```c
x86_call_depth_emit_accounting(pprog, func);
```
Reason:
The original code calls `x86_call_depth_emit_accounting` without updating the instruction pointer (`ip`). This results in the `ip` not reflecting the additional instructions emitted by the call depth accounting, leading to an incorrect offset for the subsequent `CALL` instruction. Consequently, this can cause the program to skip instructions or crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
ip += x86_call_depth_emit_accounting(pprog, func);
```
Reason:
The patch updates the `ip` variable by adding the return value of `x86_call_depth_emit_accounting`, which represents the number of bytes emitted. This ensures that the `ip` correctly accounts for the additional instructions, allowing the subsequent `CALL` instruction to have the correct offset and preventing potential instruction skipping or crashes.
